title: Protocol to Fabricate Engineered Illumination Devices for Optogenetic Control of Cellular Signaling Dynamics
protocol: Solder paste reflow soldering paste onto the copper pads on PCB-1 using the soldering mask to apply it only to the grid pattern.
Place LEDs on top of the applied solder paste according to the schematic and placement guide.
Heat the board on a hot plate to melt and solidify the solder, securing the LEDs in place.
Place surface-mount LEDs onto the pads on PCB-1 in the correct orientation.
Heat PCB-1 on a hot plate at maximum temperature for 2–5 minutes.
Inspect LED alignment and adjust with tweezers if necessary.
Wait an additional 1–2 minutes after noticing the solder paste turn metallic.
Carefully remove board from the hot plate and let cool at room temperature for 5–10 minutes.
Clean the solder mask with a paper towel.
Attach all through-hole components to PCB-1 via standard soldering techniques.
Place each component according to the marked placement on PCB-1.
Pass the leads of the component through the matching holes in the PCB.
Solder the component on the opposite side from where it is physically placed.
Ensure that each component is flush with the PCB surface.
Remove and re-solder components if they are accidentally soldered incorrectly.
Solder female headers onto PCB-1.
Remove every 4th pin from ×4 15-pin headers with pliers.
Remove every 4th pin from ×1 6-pin header with pliers.
Insert male headers into female headers, ensuring proper orientation.
Place TLC5947 LED driver through the male headers.
Ensure proper orientation of TLC5947 chip.
Solder the headers on one side of PCB-1.
Flip PCB-1 and solder the bottom leads of the headers.
Ensure correct placement of power and data transfer headers (×2 4-pin male headers).
Solder the power and data transfer headers onto PCB-1.
Solder female headers onto PCB-2.
Place male headers into the soldered female headers.
Insert Raspberry Pi Zero W through the male headers, ensuring proper orientation.
Solder the leads of the Raspberry Pi Zero W to secure it to PCB-2.
Secure PCB-2 to PCB-1 using hexagonal plastic standoffs and 2–56 screws.
Mix the two epoxy components together (1:1) for Arctic Silver thermal epoxy.
Apply a thin layer of mixed epoxy to the heat sink.
Apply a thin layer of mixed epoxy to the bare copper region of PCB-1.
Sandwich the heat sink and PCB-1 surfaces, ensuring the heat sink is centered.
Wait 1 hour or more to allow the epoxy to solidify.
Orient LAVA board base so that the indicator square faces left.
Insert rubber foot pegs into base from the bottom, through the four larger holes.
Screw vibration-damping mounts onto the base using 8–32 screws through the four smaller holes.
Screw round metal standoffs into each vibration-damping mount with an 8–32 setscrew.
Assemble and attach fan components.
Screw individual fans into the laser-cut fan holder using 6–32 screws and nuts.
Ensure the fan airflow arrow points in the correct direction.
Make sure wires face upwards.
Trim fan wires to approximately 0.5 inches (1.5 cm) in length.
Attach fan holder onto the base using right-angle brackets and 8–32 screws and nut.
Strip the end of each fan wire for approximately 3 mm.
Assemble the walls of the LED driver cover using superglue.
Cut the 80˚ LSD diffuser sheet to match the dimensions of the 3D-printed light guides.
Fit one diffuser between the two light guides, measuring 4.5 inches by 3.0 inches (11.4 cm x 7.6 cm).
Fit another diffuser for the top light guide, measuring 4.8 inches by 3.3 inches (12.2 cm x 8.4 cm).
Attach PCB-1 onto the ×4 metal standoffs.
Place bottom light guide onto PCB-1 and center it on the wells.
Secure the light guide to PCB-1 with ×4 8–32 screws through the screw holes, sandwiching PCB-1 in between.
Insert fan wires into the corresponding terminal block.
Ensure correct orientation of the fan wires during insertion.
Tighten set screw with a small flathead screwdriver.
Add the intermediate diffuser on top of the bottom light guide.
Sandwich the intermediate diffuser between the top and bottom light guides.
Place the final diffuser onto the top light guide.
Click together 3D-printed light guides, applying force if necessary.
Upload the device operating software to the LAVA board.
Calibrate the LED output.
Configure the provided GUI for spatiotemporal control of blue-light stimulation.
Download the OS disk image from https://github.com/LAVAboard/LAVA.
Insert a blank 8 GB micro SD card into your computer.
Download Etcher or another flash software.
Run Etcher and follow instructions to flash the OS disk image to the SD card.
Select the correct target drive that corresponds to the SD card.
Insert the micro SD card into the Raspberry Pi.
Power on the LAVA board.
Wait 1 min for the Pi to turn on.
Observe the LED light sequence change, indicating successful setup.
Power the LAVA device and connect to APPLE_PI WiFi network (password: raspberry).
Wirelessly SSH into the Pi using Terminal in Mac or BASH terminal in Windows.
Enter the command ssh pi@192.168.4.1 in the command line.
Stop the LED driver process on the Pi by entering htop in the command line.
Record the PID corresponding to the LED driver.
Execute the command "sudo kill PID".
Run the internal python calibration code by entering "python LED_calibration.py".
Record the light intensity data for each PWM with a power meter.
Generate the calibration curve where the X-axis is PWM (0-4095) and Y-axis is measured light intensity (μW/mm²).
Convert the light intensity recorded into μW/mm².
Apply a linear trend to the calibration curve and record the slope (m) and y-intercept (b).
Re-measure calibration values when the hardware layout of the LAVA board is modified.
Change the name of the WiFi network to a desired name if required.
Power the LED board and connect to the new or default WiFi network (password = raspberry).
Wirelessly SSH into Pi using specified instructions.
Configure the access point host software by editing sudo nano /etc/hostapd/hostapd.conf.
Change the ssid to the desired WiFi name without modifying other lines in the file.
Save the edited configuration file with ctrl-O and enter, then exit with ctrl-X.
Reboot the Raspberry Pi to see the new WiFi network name appear.
Turn on LAVA board and wait one minute for boot completion.
Connect to the LAVA board WiFi network (default = APPLE PI).
Set up wireless SSH connection at least once.
Select the Pi WiFi network (password = raspberry) from this point forward.
Download JarJarBlinks.jar from the provided link.
Open the JarJarBlinks application.
Choose the correct plate format in the application.
Enter the slope and y-intercept values from the LED calibration.
Configure the pattern to be uploaded.
Choose the "Const" designation for each well of interest.
Enter the light intensity I in the open column (default range from 0.0 – 20.0 μW/mm²).
Choose the "Blink" designation for each well of interest.
Enter Imin (typically 0.0) and Imax (experiment dependent).
Enter the duty cycle (percentage of time “on” per period) and period (in seconds).
Choose the "Func" designation for each well of interest.
Enter the linear or sinusoidal function parameters of interest and for desired time interval.
Select “add” function to add entered patterns.
Combine multiple functions to generate complex temporal light patterns.
Upload experiment pattern to LAVA board device by selecting “Submit and Upload” button.
Check if the pattern uploads successfully within 5 seconds.
Seed cells on recommended imaging plates from Key Resources Table.
Place seeded plate directly on the LAVA board for illumination.
Insert LAVA board with illuminated plate into the incubator for long-term culture.
Remove plate from LAVA board after illumination ends.
Perform end-point analysis such as immunostaining, flow cytometry, or transcriptomics.
